newsitem.title: ZAMBIA: ZCCM details copper sales terms.
newsitem.headline: ZCCM details copper sales terms.

text.p: Zambia Consolidated Copper Mines (ZCCM) said on Tuesday it would sell all copper under annual contracts for 1997 at the LME Copper Grade A Official Settlement price.

"The Zambia mining industry will sell all copper on the basis of their price for refined cathodes. The sellers price for refined cathodes will be the LME Copper Grade A Official Settlement price," a company spokesman said.
Customers would price on an average basis during the month following a contracted month of shipment for which a premium of $30 per tonne would be charged over the official settlement price.
They would have the option to change the quotation period to a contracted month of shipment once during the lifetime of the contract at a $5 per tonne surcharge to the tonnage affected by the change.
Surcharges for shipments to South East Asia and Japanese ports would apply in 1997 at $15 and $20 per tonne respectively.
"With regard to KBC cathode, the quality discount of $12 per tonne against the mentioned terms will also be retained for 1997," the spokesman said.
